title: Sprint 4 Reflection: What I Learned and How I Know
description: Use AI follow-up questions to separate what you know from what you were told.

questions.prompt: Draft your reflection. Cover one thing you can now do or decide that you could not at the start, what AI explained well and whether you ever checked it, what came back different from what you expected, something you half know and would be tempted to state confidently in a meeting, and whether either of the things you set aside now looks like a mistake.
questions.placeholder: Use your gap list, your learning path, your check results, and your updated Goal Plan. Name a capability, not a topic. If nothing came back different from what you expected, say what that tells you about the checks you designed.
questions.aiContext: This is the Sprint 4 reflection for Reframing Problems with AI. The participant is saying what they can now do that they could not do two weeks ago, and being honest about what they still cannot claim. Ask follow-up questions that catch a topic named in place of a capability, confidence that rests on an explanation that was never checked, and a claim marked confirmed without an independent source. Push them to name the thing they half know and would be tempted to state confidently in a meeting, and to say whether either exclusion now looks like a mistake. Do not rewrite the reflection for them.
questions.discussionPrompt: Use these questions to revise so that your reflection separates what you know from what you were told.
questions.summaryPlaceholder: Write the final version you want to submit. Include the capability you gained, what AI explained and whether you checked it, what came back different, what you half know, and whether an exclusion now looks like a mistake.
